name: ZW zero rule
summary: The legless black vertex (the scalar 0) next to a wire equals 0 times the disconnected wire.
description:
The black vertex with no legs is the empty sum, the scalar $0$. This axiom of the planar W-calculus says that a diagram multiplied by it is $0$ times a disconnected diagram: here a wire is cut into the effect $\langle 0|$ and the state $|0\rangle$, each a W-spider with no outputs. It plays the role of the [zero rule](../zero-rule/) of the ZX-calculus.

With the scalar $0$ written as a number both sides are $0$.
unchecked_reason: the black vertex without legs (the scalar 0) is not a PyZX W-spider
